e.text: A1 leads at 30.2% versus 8.4% benchmark; asking the Critic how to push further.

e.note: Reading results for A1, A2

critique.summary: Citywide targeted social from day 0, the Nike Training Club collab and early Palmer-pulled podcasts drive reach of about 30%, versus 8.4% for the benchmark, at roughly a third of the cost per adopter. Swapping the About Last Night podcast for 12 partner venues in A2 lost reach (28.5% vs 30.2%) and weakened the 10th percentile (27.3% vs 29.1%), because each $300 venue was credited with only 4–14 adopters.

findings.finding: A1 reached 30.2% (P10 29.1%) with 5320 adopters at $3.57 each; Nike Training Club ($2000, 670 adopters) is the most efficient action, and both podcasts returned about 212–237 adopters per ~$3400.
A2's 12 partner venues cost $3600 and were credited with about 4–14 adopters each, with Enish Croydon in Broad Green the weakest at 4; reach fell to 28.5% (P10 27.3%) at $3.81 per adopter.

Venues lifted Activewear and outdoor brands to 31.0% (vs 30.0%), but Football, Afrobeats and Gucci dropped to 24.3% (vs 27.7%) and Video games and sports to 24.4% (vs 27.4%) after About Last Night was cut.
The benchmark's broad social spent $10080 for 404 adopters, while targeted social at the same cost earned about 800, showing that taste-targeting roughly doubles media yield.

changes.change: Use A1 as the base: keep social:city days 0–56, collab:43A36E73 days 0–56 and both podcasts (853C9C96 on day 0, 3A30194F on day 1).
changes.why: A1 has the highest mean reach and the best 10th-percentile outcome, at the lowest cost per adopter.

changes.change: Spend the ~$1000 of remaining budget on only the top 2–3 venues, Sticks'n'Sushi Greenwich and Nando's Greenwich Cutty Sark (14 adopters each), seeded at day 0; drop Enish Croydon, Boho Cafe and The Ivy Cafe Blackheath.
changes.why: The weak venues returned 4–8 adopters per $300, far worse than podcasts or the collab.

changes.change: If more budget is freed, test a second co-branded collab or extra podcast flights aimed at the Football, Afrobeats and Gucci and Video games and sports districts.
changes.why: These districts lag at about 27% even in A1, and the collab is the cheapest source of adopters at about $3 each.

e.note: Citywide targeted social from day 0, the Nike Training Club collab and early Palmer-pulled podcasts drive reach of about 30%, versus 8.4% for the benchmark, at roughly a third of the cost per adopter. Swapping the About Last Night podcast for 12 partner venues in A2 lost reach (28.5% vs 30.2%) and weakened the 10th percentile (27.3% vs 29.1%), because each $300 venue was credited with only 4–14 adopters.

e.text: Revising A1 with the Critic's notes: top Greenwich venues and stronger reach into gaming and football districts.

e.note: Revising: Base on A1. R1: add Sticks'n'Sushi and Nando's Cutty Sark at day 0 with leftover ~$1000. R2: trim social slightly to fund a second collab (e.g. Brentford/EA FC-style) or extra podcast aimed at Football/Afrobeats and Video games districts. Stay under $20,000.

e.note: Writing the launch plan for B2

plan.headline: Chelsea FC Fan Zone & Burberry Kit Drop: projected 31% of London's natural audience (~5,460 adopters) for $19,630
plan.summary: We are betting that a Burberry co-branded limited kit drop turns the fan zone into a London fashion moment, backed by citywide social from day 0, two host-read podcast ads and two top-fit venues in Greenwich and Wandsworth. In Qloo taste data this audience over-indexes on Burberry (0.92), Monday Morning (0.92), The Champs (0.90), Sticks'n'Sushi (0.91) and Gola (0.90), and Cole Palmer and Chelsea F.C. are the main pull. In the simulation that leads to about 31% reach (29.5%–32.3%) at $3.59 per adopter, with 58% of adoption coming from word of mouth, against 8.4% for the same budget spent where the crowds are; these figures come from a simulation built on Qloo taste data and are not a guarantee.

weeks.label: Week 1 (days 55–49 before launch)
items: Launch interest-targeted social ads across London, weighted by cell fit ($10,080 spread over 56 days)
Go live with the Burberry co-brand announcement ($2,000) and lead with the limited kit drop
Air the host-read ad on Monday Morning Podcast ($3,500) and on The Champs ($3,450), both centred on Cole Palmer and Chelsea
Put posters and table cards up at Sticks'n'Sushi Greenwich and Gola Wandsworth ($300 each)

weeks.label: Weeks 2–4 (days 48–28)
items: Keep social running and shift spend toward the best-performing cells; K-pop, Uniqlo and dance is the strongest district so far
Push Burberry kit visuals and drop details in the social creative
Refresh venue posters and confirm they stay visible

weeks.label: Weeks 5–7 (days 27–7)
items: Use social to announce big match nights, such as a derby or cup game, to win over undecided fans
Tell people the drop allocation is fair and won't sell out instantly, and push the 'bring your mates' message
Mention food on site in all creative

weeks.label: Launch week (days 6–0)
items: Run a final social push and Burberry countdown
Remind diners at both venues about launch day
Open the fan zone with a big-screen match night and the kit drop

risks: All projections come from a simulation built on Qloo taste data. Real behaviour may differ.
Distance puts off outer-borough fans such as those in Kingston and Barnet. Big-match nights and social proof need to do the work there.
Hype around the kit drop could backfire if people think it will sell out instantly, so the allocation rules need to be clear.
The venues and The Champs ad deliver few adopters for their cost, so treat them as low-cost tests.
